In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shear strength of a multilayer is limited by shear in one of the individual layers.
the shear strength of Al/Ti is not limited by the strength of the interfacial region.
the Al/Ti N interface is strong, but that the Al/TIN multilayers are not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the Al/Ti interface is very weak (on the order the shear strength of Al), the Al/Ti multilayer is strong.
, although the Al/Ti/N interface has a very low shear strength, the Al/TIN multilayers have a high shear strength, and that the shear strength of the multilayers is determined by the Al layer.
shear in Al is the limiting factor in Al/TiN nanolaminates, and that the Al/N-terminated Al/TiN (001) interface has the lowest ideal shear strength of all the systems considered.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shear strength of the interfacial region is not necessarily the limiting strength of the Al-TiN system.
ab initio calculations can be used to predict the shear properties of interfaces, and that shear properties of interfaces can be used to design nanolaminates for improved strength and toughness.
